Export to mxfda Format

Source: R/export_mxfda.R
export_mxfda.Rd

Converts a result to a data frame shaped for mxfda::add_summary_function(), so the interaction curves can go into a functional data analysis, as the companion manuscript does with functional principal component analysis.

export_mxfda(result, sample_id = NULL, interaction_name = NULL)

Arguments

result

Object of class kernelcomm_result (must have significance computed)

sample_id

Character. Sample identifier (overrides object slot)

interaction_name

Character. Gene pair name (e.g., "CD274_PDCD1")

Value

A data frame with one row per bandwidth and columns sample_id, interaction_name, r (the bandwidth), sumfun (the observed statistic), csr (its value under complete spatial randomness), fundiff (sumfun - csr, which is what the manuscript plots), p_value, z_score, null_lower, null_upper and p_adjusted. p_adjusted is always present, as NA when not computed, so exports from different results always share a column set.

Bandwidth in the radius column

mxfda's spatial summary functions are indexed by a radius r. This export places the kernel bandwidth h in that column. They are not the same quantity. A radius is a hard cutoff: pairs inside contribute, pairs outside do not. A Gaussian bandwidth is a scale parameter with unbounded support: every pair contributes, weighted by distance, and a bandwidth of h draws most of its weight from within roughly h but not all of it.

The substitution is reasonable, because both index a family of nested spatial scales and that is all the downstream functional analysis needs. But curves exported this way are not interchangeable with radius-based summary functions such as Ripley's K or a pair correlation function, and should not be pooled with them. This is stated rather than assumed because the previous version of this function made the substitution silently.

Verification status

The column names here follow mxfda's documented contract for a summary function table. mxfda could not be installed in the environment where this was developed, so the round trip through mxfda::add_summary_function() has not been executed here. The test suite contains a check that runs it and is skipped when mxfda is absent; run the tests with mxfda installed to confirm.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 150
coords <- matrix(runif(2 * n), ncol = 2)
res <- multiScaleAC(coords, rnorm(n), rnorm(n), h = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2), perms = 99)
res <- compute_significance(res)

mx <- export_mxfda(res, sample_id = "RCC4_17")
head(mx)
#>   sample_id  interaction_name    r      sumfun           csr     fundiff
#> 1   RCC4_17 rnorm(n)_rnorm(n) 0.05 -0.05603632 -2.245794e-03 -0.05379053
#> 2   RCC4_17 rnorm(n)_rnorm(n) 0.10 -0.03061668 -2.726710e-04 -0.03034401
#> 3   RCC4_17 rnorm(n)_rnorm(n) 0.20 -0.01441424  8.930709e-05 -0.01450355
#>   p_value   z_score  null_lower null_upper p_adjusted
#> 1    0.93 -1.474076 -0.06513190 0.07356368         NA
#> 2    0.93 -1.385106 -0.03988630 0.04019971         NA
#> 3    0.89 -1.209579 -0.02052543 0.02367770         NA

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Downstream, in mxfda:
# mxfda_obj <- mxfda::add_summary_function(mxfda_obj, mx, metric = "bivariate")
} # }
